newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kone sees only small 1997 profit boost.
newsitem.headline: Kone sees only small 1997 profit boost.

text.p: Finnish elevator maker Kone Oy said on Friday it expected group 1997 earnings to only be somewhat better than last year.
"Kone's financial result for 1997 is only expected to improve somewhat over that of 1996," Kone said in a statement with its 1996 earnings.
In 1996, Kone's profit after financial items fell 39 percent to 124 million markka. The median of 14 analysts' forecasts was 82 million markka.
"The reorganisation of products, production and business processes continues in Europe," Kone said, adding that the impact would only be seen "after some time has elapsed." It did not elaborate.
Kone said its Italian operations would continue to be unprofitable during the early part of 1997, but were "expected to reach the break-even point before the end of the year."
"It is believed that new elevator recommendations published by the European Union will stimulate modernisation demand in EU countries," Kone said.
Looking back at 1996, Kone said its earnings had been poor.
"Causes were the significantly larger than anticipated problems in Kone's Italian subsidiaries and the prevailing low price level for new elevators in Europe," it said.
European construction markets had been stagnant during 1996 marked by weak demand for new elevators and poor price levels.
In North America, construction activity had picked up and new orders received had risen "gratifyingly" early in the year but levelled off later Kone said.
In Asia, construction had remained brisk and new orders had increased by nearly 50 percent.

Kone's net sales rose to 10.6 billion markka from 9.5 billion and almost 600 million markka of the increase stemmed from the acquisition of the German O&K Rolltreppen Group, whose figures were consolidated from July 1.
Kone's order backlog grew by 26 percent to 7.2 billion markka at the end of 1996. "The price levels for elevators in the order book remains low," it said.
